framework_rationale: The board faces a proposal to approve; SCR lets us set the situation (promotion escalation), the complication (it shifted volume and eroded margin, unevenly by category) and the resolution (a smaller, category-targeted 2026 plan) in the order a decision meeting needs

candidates.text: Our promotions are destroying value — they shift existing demand rather than create it while gross margin fell from 27.4% to 25.1% — so the board should reject the 20% budget increase and refocus the 2026 plan on Fresh and Beverages, cutting deep discounts in Household and Snacks
Promotions grew to 38% of sales but total volume grew only 2.1%, so promotions should be reviewed
Promotion returns vary by category, so the 2026 budget should be reallocated across categories at constant level

governing_thought: Our promotions are destroying value — they shift existing demand rather than create it while gross margin fell from 27.4% to 25.1% — so the board should reject the 20% budget increase and refocus the 2026 plan on Fresh and Beverages, cutting deep discounts in Household and Snacks

key_line.message: Promotions escalated sharply in FY2025: 38% of sales (from 29%) at 24% average depth (from 18%)
They shifted rather than created volume, while gross margin fell from 27.4% to 25.1%
Returns split by category: Household and Snacks destroy margin, Fresh and Beverages create it — and the marketing proposal scales the worst of them
2026 plan: no budget increase, cut depth in Household and Snacks, keep targeted promotion in Fresh and Beverages, and verify with a margin bridge and controlled tests
